the-tls-files-are-the-nodes-puppet-identity: 32-35 resolve ssldir to the params fixture override /etc/puppetlabs/puppet/ssl, 49-71 copy certs/ca.pem, certs/<certname>.pem and private_keys/<certname>.pem to /etc/rsyslog.d/tls owned syslog:syslog with 0644/0644/0600 and the dir 0755 (41-47); the probe compares exactly those bytes and modes (certname = the node's host name, puppet8node) and openssl-verifies the Puppet cert against the copied Puppet CA, which signed it; the mismatch varies only the CA file (the system bundle, which did not sign the cert), so the verdict must change, and it failed after apply as required

purpose covered: Purpose (shared rsyslog base: rsyslog + GnuTLS installed and running, the node's Puppet CA/cert/key copied where the syslog user rsyslog drops to can read them, rsyslog kept running and restarted on TLS changes) matches the baseline header comments and code. Checks test: packages + gtls driver + running/enabled; the copied files byte-identical to the Puppet identity with owner/modes and a verifying chain; rsyslog actually dropping to syslog, syslog able to read the key and nobody not (mismatch); a stopped rsyslog started by the next agent run; TLS directory drift corrected and rsyslog restarted (new PID); a TLS file change (renewal) restored and rsyslog restarted exactly once (journal start count, under local change #1, which subscribes the service to the three files; agent run showed Service refresh triggered from the ca.pem change).
